I estimated these from prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 structure and did not run any queries against the benchmark, so the numbers are judgement calls.

Three heuristics drove most of the non-N estimates:
- An edit that replaces `none` usually has a larger effect than one that replaces another operation.
- Removing an edge matters less when parallel paths exist, and more when it was the only route.
- Edits on an edge that cannot reach the output have no effect.

Pairs with no clear mechanism get most of their mass on N.
